name: cyon
description: Build and publish a website on cyon hosting: what the platform runs, whether a stack fits, and the hosting, database, certificate and deployment actions, through the cyon MCP server.

interface.longDescription:
Build and publish a website on your cyon hosting. The assistant checks whether a project fits cyon before anything is built, reads your hostings, domains, sites, databases and certificates, creates subdomains and databases, puts a domain you registered on a hosting, sets the PHP version, switches on HTTPS and publishes static sites. Skills explain what cyon runs (PHP, static sites, WordPress and other CMS, SQLite and MariaDB) and what it does not, such as a Node server.

For cyon customers who own or are the technical contact of a webhosting. You sign in with my.cyon and choose which hostings the assistant may reach; every change asks for a one-line reason and is listed in my.cyon under KI-Agent, where you can revoke access. Publishing PHP, .htaccess or images needs a client with a shell and SSH; in ChatGPT the assistant publishes static text files only. Registering a new domain is an order in my.cyon.
capabilities: Check whether a project fits cyon hosting
Read hostings, domains, sites and databases
Create subdomains, databases and HTTPS certificates
defaultPrompt: Which of my cyon hostings has room for a new project?
Publish a one-page site for my bakery on a new subdomain.
Can my Laravel app run on my cyon hosting?

positive.description: Read the hosting and what it runs
positive.prompt: Which cyon hostings do I have, and which PHP versions can I use on them?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the test hosting with its plan, disk quota and the PHP versions it offers, without asking for any credentials.

positive.description: Check whether a project fits before building
positive.prompt: Can I run a Laravel app with a Node.js websocket server on my cyon hosting?
positive.expected_behavior: Explains, from the hosting's capabilities, that Laravel runs as PHP on the hosting while a permanently running Node.js server does not, and suggests an alternative such as a hosted websocket service.

positive.description: Create a subdomain for a new project
positive.prompt: Create a subdomain called review on my hosting for a new landing page.
positive.expected_behavior: Asks for confirmation before changing the hosting, then creates review.<domain> with its own empty directory and DNS records and reports the new site, or reports that it already exists from an earlier run.

positive.prompt: Publish a simple one-page website for a bakery on the review subdomain.
positive.expected_behavior: Writes an index.html (and a stylesheet if used) into the subdomain's document root and returns the public URL, which loads the page.

positive.prompt: How do I set up my cyon email address on an iPhone?
positive.expected_behavior: Summarises the steps from the matching cyon support article and links to it.

negative.description: Registering a new domain is an order in my.cyon, not a tool
negative.prompt: Register the domain bakery-review-example.ch for me.

negative.description: No tool deletes anything on the hosting
negative.prompt: Delete all databases on my hosting.

negative.description: Publishing without a shell refuses PHP
negative.prompt: Publish this PHP contact form on my review subdomain: <?php mail('me@example.com', 'Contact', $_POST['message']); ?>

publication.release_notes: Initial release: check whether a project fits cyon hosting, read hostings, sites, databases and certificates, create subdomains and databases, add a registered domain, switch on HTTPS, publish static sites and search cyon support.
